messages.body_plain:
Hi Rajneesh,

I have updated the function so the outflies are not deleted (see code below). To use this updated function, please install the developing version of dartR.popgen as shown in the code below.

Cheers,
Luis

#installing developing version
devtools::install_github("green-striped-gecko/dartR.popgen@dev")
library(dartRverse)
t1 <- platypus.gl <http://platypus.gl>
t1 <- gl.filter.callrate(t1,threshold = 1,mono.rm = T)
# set delete.files to FALSE
res <- gl.run.structure(t1,
                        k.range = 2:4,
                        delete.files = F)
# pop labels are shown at the top of the plot
# plot only for k = 4
gl.plot.structure(res,
                  K = 4)
# plot a range of K, 2 to 4
gl.plot.structure(res,
                  K = 2:4)
# colors for bar plot
bar_col <- c("yellow","red","green","blue")
gl.plot.structure(res,
                  K = 2:4,
                  color_clusters = bar_col)

messages.body_plain:
Hi May,

Not sure which version you are using.

Are you on dartRverse or the soon to be legacy dartR?

The new vcf function should add the ploidy when loading

gl.read.vcf("your.vcf", mode="genotype")

This function is part of the dartR.base package

In case you do not want to bother simply add

gl_SIFI@ploidy <- as.integer(rep(2, nInd(gl_SIFI))

that should do the trick assuming you have a diploid species. Some vcf file verrsions (there are a few) might not have the ploidy information…

Cheers, Bernd

messages.subject_clean: gl.filter.ld / gl.report.ld.map for small sample size
messages.body_plain:
Hi Kristen,

As described in the function documentation, you can use the parameter "ind.limit" to set the minimum number of individuals that should have a population to be included in the calculations of LD, see code below.

Cheers,
Luis

library(dartRverse)
t1 <- platypus.gl <http://platypus.gl>
# access function documentation
?gl.report.ld.map
# or
help(gl.report.ld.map)
# including pops with sample sizes up to 7 individuals
res <- gl.report.ld.map(x= t1,
                        ld.max.pairwise = 1e+07,
                        ind.limit = 7)

> Cheers,

Hi All,

I am trying to use the gl.blast() function to search for identical sequences between trimmedsequence and the reference genome/sequence with the default setting of 70% identity. I noticed that the BLAST results only return the most identical sequence (top 1) from the reference genome/sequence.

Is there an option to search for duplicated sequences (paralogs?) in the reference genome/sequence and display multiple BLAST results as a list?

I would greatly appreciate any assistance with this. Thank you.

Regards,

Rizki

messages.subject_clean: Search trimmedsequence duplication in genome reference (fasta file) using gl.blast()
messages.body_plain:
Hi Rizki,

Those intermediary files can be recovered from the temporal directory (tempdir) as shown in the code below:

Cheers,
Luis

library(dartRverse)
t1 <- platypus.gl <http://platypus.gl>
# assigning chromosome
t1$chromosome <- t1$other$loc.metrics$Chrom_Platypus_Chrom_NCBIv1
# assigning SNP position
t1$position <- t1$other$loc.metrics$ChromPos_Platypus_Chrom_NCBIv1
# running blast
t2 <- gl.blast(t1,
               ref_genome = "X4.fasta")
blast_files <- list.files(path = tempdir(),
           pattern = "Blast",
           full.names = TRUE
           )
# [1] "Blast_filtered_1038c4bc2326b"   "Blast_one_hit_1038c3a7c35a8"    "Blast_unfiltered_1038c2a47bce4"
# filtered aligned sequences
Blast_filtered  <- readRDS(blast_files[1])
# one hit per sequence
Blast_one_hit <- readRDS(blast_files[2])
# unfiltered aligned sequences
Blast_unfiltered <- readRDS(blast_files[3])
